Yakama

This guide follows the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation through a selected historical account, the Nation-hosted 1855 treaty text, language teaching and a 2021 fisheries plan. The named constituent peoples, historical treaty wording and present government are related but different kinds of evidence. Pahto’s modern landscape image provides one specifically identified setting.

The photographer identifies the view as from Highway141 north of Trout Lake. The Nation’s historical land account specifically names Pahto/Mount Adams. This is a modern view of one public landscape, not proof that the camera/foreground is on reservation land, a territorial boundary, all constituent peoples or an adopted sacred-symbol interpretation. 01

Identity and context

The Yakama Nation is a contemporary confederated government with multiple constituent peoples.

Read the sources [1] yakama.com

02

A path for deeper reading

Focus the next stage of research on: Nation-published history, treaty context, languages and distinct community histories. The sources below are selected reading paths; their authorship, dates and community scope should guide how they are used.

Read the sources [1] yakama.com [2] Yakama Nation Fisheries [3] yakamafish-nsn.gov

03

Land, waterways and seasonal movement in the Nation’s account

The Nation’s history describes winter villages near waterways and movement across lowlands and higher country as foods became available. It names Pahto, also called Mount Adams, within this account. The 2009 photograph is a view from near Trout Lake, not a picture of the whole reservation or a present boundary.

Read the sources [4] Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation; site credits Carol Craig’s contributions

04

Reading the 1855 document and its separate dates

The Nation-hosted treaty text displays separate signing, ratification and proclamation dates. Its preamble names tribes and bands treated together for the document’s purposes. Selected Articles1–3 set out historical cession, reservation and resource provisions. The text alone does not establish consent, implementation or current legal entitlements.

Read the sources [5] United States and named tribes/bands,1855 text; hosted by Yakama Nation

05

Teaching and long-term resource planning

The language programme describes school and community teaching and a teacher-development approach; its dated references should guide further enquiries about what is offered now. The 2021 fisheries plan connects management with language, education and responsibilities to future generations. Its projects and objectives remain that publication’s institutional account, not an independent ecological evaluation.

Read the sources [6] Yakama Nation Language Program [2] Yakama Nation Fisheries

Yakama Nation Fisheries Strategic Plan 2021 — selected introduction and management scope ↗

The 2021 plan connects language, teaching and resource relationships with fisheries management, partnerships and restoration priorities. Its planning framework is not a measured account of every later result.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual PDF title/contents and revision line, prefacep5, introduction/managementpp9–10, and Nature and Geographic Scopep25; PDF and printed numbers coincide for these selections. Normal HTTP200 complete file retrieved; only these selected bodies read.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Web reader could not handle the21.9MB PDF, so normal download and text extraction were used. Figures, photographs, map geometry, biological tables, current staff/species totals, legal holdings and the rest of the document were not inspected or reproduced. Source-specific copyright photos remain excluded. Plans/claims are attributed to the 2021 publication, not treated as current ecological outcomes.

Treaty of 1855 — Nation-hosted text, selected preamble and Articles1–3 ↗

The reproduced preamble names participating tribes and bands; selected articles set out cession, reservation and fishing/gathering provisions. These are historical textual terms, not proof of implementation or present boundaries.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual displayed dates, preamble and complete Articles1–3, web lines35–49.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Original signed manuscript, translation, negotiations, assent, implementation and later case law not independently inspected. Historical wording is retained at the source, not converted into current legal advice or mapped boundaries.
